instruction.text: Get to know these people by filling in the gaps.

atoms.b: Nora is pregnant and can regularly go to see her ((++doctor florist)).
Louis works in a supermarket and earns enough money to live ((++normally lavishly)).
Tham can go to school every day and ((++learn buy)) new things.
People have rights! Nora, Louis, Tham and everyone else in the world have a ((++right_to desire_for)) all of these things.

instruction.text: What do we call the rights that everyone has?
Human rights were agreed upon and written down by an organisation made up of almost all the countries in the world. In which book do you think human rights were recorded?

b.sound: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights

instruction.text: Read this summarised version of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and then fill in the gaps.
instruction.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='de' voice='custom'>book-page</voice> Read this summarised version of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and then fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Human rights help us to be treated fairly, to live ((++freely under_restriction)) and to live safely.

instruction.text: Children do not just have human rights but also other additional rights. What do you think these rights are called? Select the correct answer.
In the UK, from what age is someone no-longer a child? Select the correct age.

feedback.end: There are also some countries where people stop being a child earlier or later than 18.

instruction.text: Each person is labelled with their age. Which people still have children’s rights? Select all the children.

hint.text: In the UK, you are legally a child until you turn 18.

instruction.text: Why do children need their own rights? Select the two correct answers.

b: ++Children need special protection in order to develop well.
++Children need special protection from exploitation and abuse by adults.
Children are smaller than adults and need an advantage.

instruction.text: Why do you think it is important to know about children’s rights? Select the two correct answers.

b: ++So that it is easier to recognise when these rights are being violated.
++So you can make your own decisions and look after your own interests.
So you can take away the rights of children.
